source.title: Extrapolation for Large-batch Training in Deep Learning
source.authors: Tao Lin; Lingjing Kong; Sebastian U. Stich; Martin Jaggi

record.file_problem: none; full paper text and appendices are present
record.tranche_reason: Compares held-out perplexity across two global batch sizes at a fixed 300-epoch budget, using the paper’s extrapolation method alongside mini-batch SGD.
record.gate_note: The study also reports many comparisons among extrapolation methods at a fixed batch size; those do not test the mapped claim versions and are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares held-out perplexity at two global batch sizes under the same 300-epoch budget. Its own WikiText-2 results test V5, beyond evaluating its proposed optimizer.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors attribute the main benefits to faster early optimization and better-conditioned trajectories; learning-rate decay diminishes the advantage, and smoothing does not guarantee a substantially better final minimum. Combining extrapolation with post-local SGD improves large-batch results.
record.recipe_differences: Uses extrapolation with past local mini-batch gradients, alongside mini-batch SGD, rather than testing the original large-batch interventions as a replication.
record.method_sensitivity: For the tested WikiText-2 LSTM, validation PPL is higher at K = 48 than at K = 24 for both mini-batch SGD and EXTRAP-SGD.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 1(b) measures gradient Lipschitz smoothness along update directions and reports improved smoothness with EXTRAP-SGD.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Extrapolation can improve local optimization smoothness; this does not measure V7's magnitude-aware sharpness or its ranking of generalization gaps.

record.code_released: not stated; the paper says the code is included in the submission for reproducibility
record.problems: Only one language-model architecture and dataset are used for the batch-size comparison, at two batch sizes. Image-classification results do not provide a corresponding global-batch-size comparison at a fixed epoch budget.
record.rows_left_out: No additional results bearing on a mapped version were omitted. The image-classification batch-size results do not compare different global batch sizes at a fixed epoch budget.

untested.parts: Generalization when widening beyond the width needed to interpolate.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under comparable tuning.

The recorded rows do not test whether longer training, normalization changes, or regularization changes remove the batch-size penalty. They do not establish the threshold where degradation begins or isolate the benefit of scaling and warmup.
The effect of adding or removing dropout; dropout settings are specified but not experimentally contrasted.
Magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance, its association with training–test gaps, and comparison with norm- and margin-based rankings.
Removing highly memorized examples versus removing random examples.

missing.what: Figure 3 also contains cross-batch validation perplexity and accuracy curves for Adam and EXTRAP-Adam on Multi30k at K = 20 and K = 80. Extract matched-epoch comparisons before deciding their direction; the supplied text does not preserve readable curve values. This is an additional potential V5 comparison on a translation task.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for V5. The two recorded batch comparisons support a penalty despite scaling and warmup, but do not establish a universal penalty or a separate generalization mechanism: held-out degradation can include optimization effects. Fixed-batch method comparisons in Tables 1–3 do not by themselves establish a batch-size penalty. Figure 4 discusses longer training at batch 16,384, but the supplied plot text lacks readable endpoints and a matched small-batch reference.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and generalization on natural labels.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under different tuning or decay recipes.
Image-classifier batch-size comparisons at a fixed epoch budget; language-model comparisons beyond the two tested batch sizes; normalization or regularization changes as batch size varies.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to the generalization gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring test accuracy.
